items.title: The One Number Cisco Stock Investors Should Watch
items.summary: You probably think of Cisco Systems (CSCO) as an AI stock, a supplier of AI infrastructure to the hyperscalers. That business was only about 6% of Cisco's revenue in fiscal 2026. The rest includes networking and security products sold to enterprises and telcos. Cisco stock returned 61% over the past year. With AI that small a share of revenue, you are paying for growth across the whole company. How fast is Cisco's business outside AI set to grow.

items.title: BlackBerry Advances 5% on Continued QNX Momentum; Palo Alto Networks Gains 4%, CrowdStrike Edges Up 2%
items.summary: BlackBerry's QNX unit just landed its biggest automotive design win ever, and the ripple pushed the stock sharply higher alongside major cybersecurity names, but the real question is how long before that deal actually shows up in revenue.

items.title: Is CrowdStrike Stock Paying You Enough For The Swings?
items.summary: You may own CrowdStrike (CRWD), a cybersecurity company whose shares rose 5.1% in five sessions as the S&P 500 fell 1.2%. You likely hold it beside an index fund, and your whole account swings more when one holding jumps. Have the gains on CrowdStrike been big enough to pay for those swings.

items.title: All In On Cybersecurity: The Choice Between Palo Alto Networks or Crowdstrike Not Difficult
items.summary: Palo Alto and CrowdStrike both reported blockbuster quarters and both credit AI for pushing cybersecurity to the top of every CIO's budget. But their strategies, valuations, and risk profiles point in opposite directions, and only one of them offers a compelling entry point right now.

items.title: Palo Alto CEO Said The Quiet Part About AI Aloud And I Buy Reality
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora said something on the earnings call that most tech executives only whisper, and it tells you exactly why one investor keeps adding to his position despite a nine-figure GAAP loss.
